sa: य एको जालवान् ईशत ईशनीभिः सर्वांल् लोकान् ईशत ईशनीभिः  ।
य एवैक उद्भवे संभवे च य एतद् विदुर् अमृतास् ते भवन्ति ॥
iast: ya eko jālavān īśata īśanībhiḥ sarvāṃl lokān īśata īśanībhiḥ  ।
ya evaika udbhave saṃbhave ca ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti ॥
words: furnished with a net; covered with iron net-work; furnished with lattice-windows

tr.text: It is the self-same One who exists alone at the time of creation and dissolution of the universe, that assumes manifold powers and appears as the Divine Lord by virtue of His inscrutable power of Maya. He it is that protects all the worlds and controls all the various forces working therein. Those who realize this Being becomes immortal.

sa: एको हि रुद्रो न द्वितीयाय तस्थे य इमांल् लोकान् ईशत ईशनीभिः  ।
प्रत्यङ् जनास् तिष्ठति संचुकोचान्तकाले संसृज्य विश्वा भुवनानि गोपाः ॥
iast: eko hi rudro na dvitīyāya tasthe ya imāṃl lokān īśata īśanībhiḥ  ।
pratyaṅ janās tiṣṭhati saṃcukocāntakāle saṃsṛjya viśvā bhuvanāni gopāḥ ॥
words: to shrink; to close (as a flower); to contract

tr.text: He who protects and controls the worlds by His own powers, He – Rudra – is indeed one only. There is no one beside Him who can make Him the second. O men, He is present inside the hearts of all beings. After projecting and maintaining all the worlds, He finally withdraws them into Himself.

sa: विश्वतश्चक्षुर् उत विश्वतोमुखो विश्वतोबाहुर् उत विश्वतस्पात्  ।
सं बाहुभ्यां धमति सं पतत्रैर् द्यावाभूमी जनयन् देव एकः ॥
iast: viśvataścakṣur uta viśvatomukho viśvatobāhur uta viśvataspāt  ।
saṃ bāhubhyāṃ dhamati saṃ patatrair dyāvābhūmī janayan deva ekaḥ ॥
words: facing all sides; one whose face is turned everywhere
one who has arms on every side
the arm; the fore-arm; the arm between the elbow and the wrist (opp. to pra-gaṇḍa)

tr.text: Though God, the creator of heaven and earth, is one only, yet Heaven is the real owner of all the eyes, faces, hands and feet in this universe. It is Heaven who inspires them all to do their respective duties in accordance with the knowledge, past actions and tendencies of the various beings (with whom they appear to be associated).

sa: यो देवानां प्रभवश् चोद्भवश् च विश्वाधिपो रुद्रो महर्षिः  ।
हिरण्यगर्भं जनयामास पूर्वं स नो बुद्ध्या शुभया संयुनक्तु ॥
iast: yo devānāṃ prabhavaś codbhavaś ca viśvādhipo rudro maharṣiḥ  ।
hiraṇyagarbhaṃ janayāmāsa pūrvaṃ sa no buddhyā śubhayā saṃyunaktu ॥
words: name of the god of tempests and father and ruler of the Rudras and Maruts
being before or in front fore
the power of forming and retaining conceptions and general notions

tr.text: May Heaven, who created the gods and supports them; who is the origin also of the cosmic soul; who confers bliss and wisdom on the devotes, destroying their sins and sorrows, and punishing all breaches of law – may Heaven, the great seer and the lord of all, endow us with good thoughts.

sa: या ते रुद्र शिवा तनूर् अघोरापापकाशिनी  ।
तया नस् तनुवा शंतमया गिरिशन्ताभिचाकशीहि ॥
iast: yā te rudra śivā tanūr aghorāpāpakāśinī  ।
tayā nas tanuvā śaṃtamayā giriśantābhicākaśīhi ॥
words: (only ifc.) shining; appearing; having the semblance of
most beneficent or wholesome or salutary; wohlt￤tig

tr.text: O Lord, who blesses all creatures by revealing the Vedas, deign to make us happy by Thy calm and blissful self, which roots out terror as well as sin.

sa: याम् इषुं गिरिशन्त हस्ते बिभर्ष्य् अस्तवे  ।
शिवां गिरित्र तां कुरु मा हिंसीः पुरुषं जगत् ॥
iast: yām iṣuṃ giriśanta haste bibharṣy astave  ।
śivāṃ giritra tāṃ kuru mā hiṃsīḥ puruṣaṃ jagat ॥
words: (in mathematics) a versed sine; name of a Soma ceremony; the number five

tr.text: O revealer of the Vedic truths, deign to make propitious that arrow which Thou holdest in Thy hand for shooting at somebody. O protector of devotees, do not destroy that benign personal form of Thine which has manifested as the universe.

sa: ततः परं ब्रह्म परं बृहन्तं यथानिकायं सर्वभूतेषु गूढं  ।
विश्वस्यैकं परिवेष्टितारम् ईशं तं ज्ञात्वामृता भवन्ति ॥
iast: tataḥ paraṃ brahma paraṃ bṛhantaṃ yathānikāyaṃ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍhaṃ  ।
viśvasyaikaṃ pariveṣṭitāram īśaṃ taṃ jñātvāmṛtā bhavanti ॥

tr.text: Higher than this Personal Brahman is the infinite Supreme Brahman, who is concealed in all beings according to their bodies, and who, though remaining single, envelops the whole universe. Knowing him to be the Lord, one becomes immortal.

sa: वेदाहम् एतं पुरुषं महान्तम् आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात्  ।
तम् एव विदित्वाति मृत्युम् एति नान्यः पन्था विद्यते ऽयनाय ॥
iast: vedāham etaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt  ।
tam eva viditvāti mṛtyum eti nānyaḥ panthā vidyate ’yanāya ॥

tr.text: I have realized this Great Being who shines effulgent like the sun beyond all darkness. One passes beyond death only on realizing Him. There is no other way of escape from the circle of births and deaths.

sa: यस्मात् परं नापरम् अस्ति किंचिद् यस्मान् नाणीयो न ज्यायो ऽस्ति किंचित्  ।
वृक्ष इव स्तब्धो दिवि तिष्ठत्य् एकस् तेनेदं पूर्णं पुरुषेण सर्वम् ॥
iast: yasmāt paraṃ nāparam asti kiṃcid yasmān nāṇīyo na jyāyo ’sti kiṃcit  ।
vṛkṣa iva stabdho divi tiṣṭhaty ekas tenedaṃ pūrṇaṃ puruṣeṇa sarvam ॥

tr.text: There is naught higher than or different from Him; naught greater or more minute than Him. Rooted in His own glory He stands like a tree, one without a second and immovable. By that Being the whole universe is filled.

sa: ततो यद् उत्तरतरं यद् अरूपम् अनामयम्  ।
य एतद् विदुर् अमृतास् ते भवन्ति अथेतरे दुःखम् एवापियन्ति ॥
iast: tato yad uttarataraṃ yad arūpam anāmayam  ।
ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti athetare duḥkham evāpiyanti ॥
words: still further removed; still more distant; still higher

tr.text: That Being is far beyond this world, is formless and free from misery. They who know this become immortal. But all others have indeed to suffer misery alone.

sa: सर्वाननशिरोग्रीवः सर्वभूतगुहाशयः  ।
सर्वव्यापी स भगवांस् तस्मात् सर्वगतः शिवः ॥
iast: sarvānanaśirogrīvaḥ sarvabhūtaguhāśayaḥ  ।
sarvavyāpī sa bhagavāṃs tasmāt sarvagataḥ śivaḥ ॥
words: the back part of the neck

tr.text: Therefore, that Divine Lord, being all-pervading, omnipresent and benevolent, dwells in the hearts of all beings, and makes use of all faces, heads and necks in this world.

sa: महान् प्रभुर् वै पुरुषः सत्त्वस्यैष प्रवर्तकः  ।
सुनिर्मलाम् इमां प्राप्तिम् ईशानो ज्योतिर् अव्ययः ॥
iast: mahān prabhur vai puruṣaḥ sattvasyaiṣa pravartakaḥ  ।
sunirmalām imāṃ prāptim īśāno jyotir avyayaḥ ॥

tr.text: This Self is indeed the mighty Lord. He is the imperishable (internal) light that controls everything. He guides the intellect of all beings so as to enable them to gain that extremely pure state (of Mukti).

sa: अङ्गुष्ठमात्रः पुरुषो ऽन्तरात्मा सदा जनानां हृदये संनिविष्टः  ।
हृदा मनीषा मनसाभिकॢप्तो य एतद् विदुर् अमृतास् ते भवन्ति ॥
iast: aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ puruṣo ’ntarātmā sadā janānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭaḥ  ।
hṛdā manīṣā manasābhikḷpto ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti ॥
words: the heart (or region of the heart as the seat of feelings and sensations)
to sit or settle down together with
the heart (as the seat of feelings and emotions)
mind (in its widest sense as applied to all the mental powers)

tr.text: Assuming a form of the size of a thumb, by virtue of intellect, emotion, imagination and will, the Infinite Being dwells in the hearts of creatures as their inner self. Those who realize this become immortal.

sa: सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुषः सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात्  ।
स भूमिं विश्वतो वृत्वा अत्यतिष्ठद् दशाङ्गुलम् ॥
iast: sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt  ।
sa bhūmiṃ viśvato vṛtvā atyatiṣṭhad daśāṅgulam ॥
words: to be at the head of

tr.text: That Infinite Being has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes and a thousand feet enveloping the whole universe on all sides. He exists beyond ten fingers.

sa: पुरुष एवेदं सर्वं यद् भूतं यच् च भव्यम्  ।
उतामृतत्वस्येशानो यद् अन्नेनातिरोहति ॥
iast: puruṣa evedaṃ sarvaṃ yad bhūtaṃ yac ca bhavyam  ।
utāmṛtatvasyeśāno yad annenātirohati ॥

tr.text: That which is, that which was, and that which is yet to be – all this is nothing but this Infinite Being. Though He grows beyond His own nature into the form of the objective universe, He still remains the lord of immortality.

sa: सर्वतःपाणिपादं तत् सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखं  ।
सर्वतःश्रुतिमल् लोके सर्वम् आवृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
iast: sarvataḥpāṇipādaṃ tat sarvato’kṣiśiromukhaṃ  ।
sarvataḥśrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati ॥

tr.text: With hands and feet everywhere, with eyes, heads and mouths everywhere, with ears everywhere, That exists, pervading everything in the universe.

sa: सर्वेन्द्रियगुणाभासं सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जितं  ।
सर्वस्य प्रभुम् ईशानं सर्वस्य शरणं सुहृत् ॥
iast: sarvendriyaguṇābhāsaṃ sarvendriyavivarjitaṃ  ।
sarvasya prabhum īśānaṃ sarvasya śaraṇaṃ suhṛt ॥
words: a single thread or strand of a cord or twine

tr.text: They realize Him as shining by the functions of all the senses yet without the senses as the lord of all, the ruler of all, the refuge of all and the friend of all.

sa: नवद्वारे पुरे देही हंसो लेलायते बहिः  ।
वशी सर्वस्य लोकस्य स्थावरस्य चरस्य च ॥
iast: navadvāre pure dehī haṃso lelāyate bahiḥ  ।
vaśī sarvasya lokasya sthāvarasya carasya ca ॥

tr.text: It is He who resides in the body, the city of nine gates. He is the soul that sports in the outside world. He is the master of the whole world, animate and inanimate.

sa: अपाणिपादो जवनो ग्रहीता पश्यत्य् अचक्षुः स शृणोत्य् अकर्णः  ।
स वेत्ति वेद्यं न च तस्यास्ति वेत्ता तम् आहुर् अग्र्यं पुरुषं महान्तम् ॥
iast: apāṇipādo javano grahītā paśyaty acakṣuḥ sa śṛṇoty akarṇaḥ  ।
sa vetti vedyaṃ na ca tasyāsti vettā tam āhur agryaṃ puruṣaṃ mahāntam ॥
words: ono who knows or feels or witnesses or experiences

tr.text: Without hands and feet He goes fast and grasps; without eyes He sees; without ears He hears. He knows whatever is to be known, yet there is none who knows Him. They say He is the foremost, the great Infinite Being.

sa: अणोर् अणीयान् महतो महीयान् आत्मा गुहायां निहितो ऽस्य जन्तोः  ।
तम् अक्रतुं पश्यति वीतशोको धातुप्रसादान् महिमानम् ईशम् ॥
iast: aṇor aṇīyān mahato mahīyān ātmā guhāyāṃ nihito ’sya jantoḥ  ।
tam akratuṃ paśyati vītaśoko dhātuprasādān mahimānam īśam ॥

tr.text: Subtler than even the subtlest and greater than the greatest, the Atman is concealed in the heart of the creature. By the grace of the Creator, one becomes free from sorrows and desires, and then realizes Him as the great Lord.

sa: वेदाहम् एतम् अजरं पुराणं सर्वात्मानं सर्वगतं विभुत्वात्  ।
जन्मनिरोधं प्रवदन्ति यस्य ब्रह्मवादिनो हि प्रवदन्ति नित्यम् ॥
iast: vedāham etam ajaraṃ purāṇaṃ sarvātmānaṃ sarvagataṃ vibhutvāt  ।
janmanirodhaṃ pravadanti yasya brahmavādino hi pravadanti nityam ॥

tr.text: I know this undecaying primeval Immanent Self of all, who is omnipresent because of His allpervasiveness, and whom the expounders of Brahman declare to be eternally free from birth.
